content.intro: Learn queryset performance optimization through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: QuerySet Performance Optimization matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines queryset performance optimization as part of the django orm and querysets. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: select_related(); prefetch_related(); Query count reduction; Avoiding N+1 query problems; Inspecting generated SQL and execution plans. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: select_related()
items.text: `select_related()` joins single-valued relations in a query; `prefetch_related()` performs separate queries and joins results in Python for multi-valued relationships. Measure the actual workload.

items.title: prefetch_related()
items.text: For prefetch_related(), identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Query count reduction
items.text: Query count reduction should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

items.title: Avoiding N+1 query problems

items.title: Inspecting generated SQL and execution plans
items.text: Inspecting generated SQL and execution plans affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.
